samples.summary: New `YorkieDocStore(doc, readOnly)` presence gate has no test, although the sibling spreadsheet gate got a whole new suite
samples.evidence: The diff adds a `readOnly` constructor arg to `YorkieDocStore` and two new early-returns that suppress presence writes (`publishResolvedLocalCursor` ~line 1260 and `updateCursorPos` ~line 3193). `packages/frontend/tests/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.test.ts` contains no occurrence of `readOnly` (grep for `readOnly` in that file: no matches), and every `new YorkieDocStore(doc)` call in tests uses the one-arg form, so the writable default is exercised but the guarded path never is. The analogous spreadsheet gate did get `tests/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-store-read-only.test.ts` counting `doc.update` calls — the same technique is directly applicable here. If this guard regresses (or over-fires), a share-link viewer's own sync wedges on their first click, or editors lose cursor presence — both user-visible, and nothing in the suite would notice.

samples.summary: Read-only presence gates in slides-view, board-view and pdf-collab's activePage publish are untested
samples.evidence: The diff adds `if (readOnlyMount) return;` to the slides `broadcast`, `if (readOnly) return;` to `board-view`'s `onSelectionChange` presence publish, and `readOnly ||` to `pdf-collab`'s `onActivePageChange`. Grepping packages/frontend/tests for `readOnlyMount`, `updatePresence`, `onActivePageChange`/`activePage` returns nothing covering these; the only component tests near them (`pdf-collab.test.tsx`) always pass `readOnly={false}`, and the new `pdf-collab-provider.test.tsx` covers only `initialRoot`, not the page-broadcast gate. These are the same class of guard as the tested spreadsheet/store gates, but at the component level, so a regression (presence published on a viewer mount, wedging their sync) ships undetected.

The diff changes the initial cross-sheet recalc from `runRemoteSync(true)` to `runRemoteSync(!readOnly)` and gates the remote-change handler on `readOnly`. No frontend test mounts `SheetView` (no file under packages/frontend/tests references `sheet-view`), and the new `yorkie-store-read-only.test.ts` covers only the store, not this call site. A regression here either re-introduces a viewer write (sync wedge) or drops recalculation for editors (stale cached formula values shown), neither caught by the suite.

samples.summary: New read-only early-return in `Spreadsheet.recalculateCrossSheetFormulas` has no test in packages/sheets
samples.evidence: The diff adds `if (this._readOnly) { this.worksheet.render(); return; }`. packages/sheets/test contains no construction of the `Spreadsheet` view class at all (grep `new Spreadsheet(`/`createSpreadsheet`: no matches) and `recalculateCrossSheetFormulas` appears only in model-level tests (`test/sheet/cross-sheet-*.test.ts`) that call `Sheet.recalculateCrossSheetFormulas` directly, bypassing the new gate. So the claim 'refuses it at the engine too, so neither this call site nor a future one can leak it' is asserted only in a comment.

samples.summary: `CommentPopover`'s new `readOnly` prop (and the new signed-in view-only message) is untested
samples.evidence: `isReadOnly = readOnly || currentUser === null` and the branched empty-state copy are new behavior; grepping packages/frontend for `CommentPopover` finds only source files (sheet-view.tsx, yorkie-store.ts, the component itself, docs equivalents) and no test file. The store-level `assertWritable` throws are tested in the new `yorkie-store-read-only.test.ts`, so the failure mode of an untested UI gate is contained (a signed-in viewer sees affordances that then throw), but the affordance-hiding itself has no coverage.

samples.summary: `sideTokenInjector` (per-side secret, no cross-fallback) has no test, though the no-fallback rule is the security property the doc-comment stresses
samples.evidence: The new `sideTokenInjector(side, envVar)` reads only its own env var and must never fall back to the other side's or to `process.env.JWT_SECRET`. There is no spec for `packages/backend/scripts/*` (backend jest specs live under src/**/*.spec.ts; the node:test lane covers scripts/agent only), and `auth.service.spec.ts` only covers `signYorkieServiceToken`/`yorkieServiceTokenInjector` generically. A regression that introduced a fallback would send deployment A's all-documents credential to deployment B with nothing failing.

samples.summary: The 'no secret ⇒ undefined injector (anonymous attach) + warn' branch of `yorkieServiceTokenInjector` / `yorkieServiceTokenInjectorFromEnv` is untested
samples.evidence: `auth.service.spec.ts` only calls `yorkieServiceTokenInjector('access-secret')` and asserts it is defined; nothing exercises `yorkieServiceTokenInjector(undefined)` returning `undefined`, nor `yorkieServiceTokenInjectorFromEnv()` with `JWT_SECRET` unset. `yorkie.service.spec.ts`'s mock config always returns a secret, so the parallel `YorkieService` warn-branch is also uncovered. Failure is loud-ish (denied attach), hence minor.

samples.summary: The layout's 'no localStorage writes' promise is only asserted for viewMode, not keymap/showAuthors
samples.evidence: The doc-comment says the state is 'the workspace route's, minus every `localStorage` **write**', but only `applies a view-mode change without persisting it` checks a key (`wafflebase:notes:viewMode`). `setKeymap`/`setShowAuthors` are passed straight to the toolbar and never asserted to leave `wafflebase:notes:keymap` / show-authors preferences untouched, so an anonymous visitor overwriting a browser preference through those controls would pass.
searchedFor: read the new shared-notes-layout.test.tsx in the diff
grep readKeymap/readShowAuthors usage in the new layout

samples.summary: 'hands the share-token uploader to the view' largely asserts the mock it installed
samples.evidence: `shareTokenImageUploader` is mocked to `(token) => async () => `uploaded:${token}``, and the test asserts the resolved value is `uploaded:tok-1`. The only real behavior verified is that the layout calls the factory with `token` and forwards the result under the `uploadImage` prop — the uploader itself and NotesView's use of it are mocked away. The companion viewer assertion (`uploadImage` undefined) is the load-bearing half.
searchedFor: grep image-insert mock in the test

finding.summary: `Spreadsheet.recalculateCrossSheetFormulas` read-only early-return is untested, and so is `sheet-view`'s `runRemoteSync(!readOnly)` gate
finding.evidence: The diff adds `if (this._readOnly) { this.worksheet.render(); return; }` to `Spreadsheet.recalculateCrossSheetFormulas` and calls it the engine-level backstop ('so neither this call site nor a future one can leak it'). `grep recalculateCrossSheetFormulas packages/sheets` shows tests only for `Sheet.recalculateCrossSheetFormulas` (test/sheet/cross-sheet-*.test.ts), none constructing a read-only `Spreadsheet`; the only read-only view test, test/view/worksheet-readonly-editing.test.ts, covers `finishEditing` only. Frontend-side, `runRemoteSync(!readOnly)` and `scheduleRemoteSync(readOnly ? false : …)` in sheet-view.tsx have no test either (no sheet-view test file). A regression re-enables a viewer's recalc write, which the webhook refuses and which wedges that viewer's sync — the exact failure this change exists to prevent.
